chapter: Technique, New Orleans influence and the school's future
title: Can the New Orleans tradition be perpetuated by a school?
summary: Ed Lewis asks whether the art form can survive; DeVore says only partly, since the way of life is gone, and the tape closes.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Yeah. That is the whole idea of the school is to perpetuate an art form. Do you think it's still possible?

Well it's obvious. I don't think you can do it with color. It's like that old question. I don't think the younger color ones will want to. Well it's obvious it's going to have to be divorced from the environment that first posted this music. Do you think it can still be done?

Yeah, to a point. Like I say it'll never be exactly the way the guys did it. No, I don't think no matter how hard a guy tries it just can't. You'll never have quite that. It's undefinable because it's there but you don't know what it is that makes their music just a little bit more distinct than a band assimilating the style. From just the musical angles. It's a way of life. That way of life no longer exists. Therefore you're not going to have the music exactly like the way it was. I'm afraid that's it.
But really it hasn't been the end of it. How did you say that?
